data.name: Alistair
data.gender_notes: Alistair is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Scottish 'Alistair mac Gilleis', meaning 'Ruler of the people'. This ancient name was popularized in Scotland by Saint Alistair, a 13th-century bishop who established the Diocese of Moray. The name Alistair carries the meaning “Ruler of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Alistair usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alistair total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

In modern Christian cultures, Alistair remains a popular choice for parents seeking a name that reflects divine guardianship and spiritual strength.
